# Card

A structural surface for related content without ambiguous interactive behavior.

## Usage

```js
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Security report</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Updated five minutes ago</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>No critical findings were detected.</CardContent>
</Card>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Related content needs a structural surface.
### Avoid when

A card is being used only to decorate every section or hide a primary action.
### Behavior

Card is non-interactive by default and accepts an explicit polymorphic element.
### Responsive

Use compact padding and let card content define its width.

## Examples

### Composition

Cards compose header, content, and footer regions with consistent rhythm.

```jsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@kryv/teal'

export function CardDemo() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-md">
      <CardHeader className="flex-col items-start justify-start gap-1.5">
        <CardTitle>Security report</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Updated five minutes ago</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface">No critical findings were detected.</p>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button size="sm" variant="secondary">
          View report
        </Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

### Report summary

Use a card to group a short summary and one related action.

```jsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@kryv/teal'

export function CardDemo() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-md">
      <CardHeader className="flex-col items-start justify-start gap-1.5">
        <CardTitle>Security report</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Updated five minutes ago</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface">No critical findings were detected.</p>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button size="sm" variant="secondary">
          View report
        </Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Card

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Applies disabled styling and blocks interaction on interactive cards. |
| `type` | `enum` | - | Button type used when the card renders an interactive element. |
| `as` | `ElementType` | `div` | - |

### CardHeader

_This module forwards native element properties._

### CardTitle

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `titleAs` | `enum` | `"h2"` | Heading element used for the title; defaults to 'h2'. Adjust to fit the page outline. |

### CardDescription

_This module forwards native element properties._

### CardContent

_This module forwards native element properties._

### CardFooter

_This module forwards native element properties._

## Accessibility

- Cards are passive surfaces with no keyboard behavior of their own.
- Render real links and buttons inside a card rather than making the card itself clickable.
- The as prop lets you render the card as a section, article, or list item to fit the page outline.
- Disabled cards are dimmed, skip pointer events, and set aria-disabled.
- CardTitle renders an h2 by default; set titleAs so card headings fit the surrounding page outline.

---

# Launcher Card

An interactive application destination card with an icon, description, optional status, and an honest unavailable state.

## Usage

```js
import { LauncherCard, Badge } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<LauncherCard
  href="https://photos.example"
  label="Photos"
  description="Household media, albums, and sharing"
  icon={<Camera />}
  status={<Badge variant="success">Healthy</Badge>}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

An application destination needs a prominent, scannable entry point.
### Avoid when

The destination is a minor link inside prose; use a plain link instead.
### Behavior

Disabled cards leave the focus order and block navigation instead of hiding.
### Responsive

Cards stack single-column on mobile and grid at larger widths under the caller’s layout.

## Examples

### Available application

The whole card navigates; status content stays caller-supplied and sanitized.

```jsx
import { Badge, LauncherCard } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Camera } from 'lucide-react'

export function LauncherCardDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <LauncherCard
      href="https://trict.kryvlabs.example"
      label="Trict"
      description="Trading research and execution"
      disabled
    />
  ) : (
    <LauncherCard
      href="https://photos.kryvlabs.example"
      label="Photos"
      description="Household media, albums, and sharing"
      icon={<Camera />}
      status={<Badge variant="success">Healthy</Badge>}
    />
  )
}
```

### Unavailable application

A disabled card is removed from focus order and blocks navigation.

```jsx
import { Badge, LauncherCard } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Camera } from 'lucide-react'

export function LauncherCardDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <LauncherCard
      href="https://trict.kryvlabs.example"
      label="Trict"
      description="Trading research and execution"
      disabled
    />
  ) : (
    <LauncherCard
      href="https://photos.kryvlabs.example"
      label="Photos"
      description="Household media, albums, and sharing"
      icon={<Camera />}
      status={<Badge variant="success">Healthy</Badge>}
    />
  )
}
```

---

# Badge

A compact semantic status indicator using canonical information variants.

## Usage

```js
import { Badge } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Badge variant="success">Deployed</Badge>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A short status or category needs quick visual scanning.
### Avoid when

The content needs an action or a sentence of explanation.
### Behavior

Variant changes meaning without changing the content semantics.
### Responsive

Keep labels short so badges do not dominate dense rows.

## Examples

### Variants

Five variants cover neutral, informational, success, warning, and danger statuses.

```jsx
import { Badge } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BadgeDemo() {
  return (
    <>
      <Badge>Neutral</Badge>
      <Badge variant="info">Information</Badge>
      <Badge variant="success">Ready</Badge>
      <Badge variant="warning">Attention</Badge>
      <Badge variant="danger">Action required</Badge>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Table statuses

Keep status text explicit when badges appear in dense data rows.

```jsx
import { Badge } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BadgeDemo() {
  return (
    <>
      <Badge>Neutral</Badge>
      <Badge variant="info">Information</Badge>
      <Badge variant="success">Ready</Badge>
      <Badge variant="warning">Attention</Badge>
      <Badge variant="danger">Action required</Badge>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Badge

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| null` | `"neutral"` | Semantic color treatment. |

## Accessibility

- Badges are plain text, so their status is announced verbatim by screen readers.
- Always pair a variant with meaningful text; never rely on color alone to carry the status.

---

# Accordion

A stacked disclosure list with single and multi-open modes driven by a compact item interface.

## Usage

```js
import { Accordion } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Accordion
  defaultValue="sign-in"
  items={[
    { value: 'sign-in', title: 'Sign-in notifications', content: 'Get alerted when a new device signs in.' },
    { value: 'sessions', title: 'Active sessions', content: 'Review and revoke sessions.' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Sections of related content should be progressively disclosed.
### Avoid when

All content must be visible at once or sections are compared side by side.
### Behavior

Single mode keeps at most one item open and is collapsible; multiple mode opens any number.
### Responsive

Keep titles short so triggers stay on one line.

## Examples

### Single-open

At most one item is open, and the open item can be collapsed again.

```jsx
import { Accordion } from '@kryv/teal'

const securityItems = [
  {
    value: 'sign-in',
    title: 'Sign-in notifications',
    content: 'Get alerted when a new device signs in to your account.',
  },
  {
    value: 'sessions',
    title: 'Active sessions',
    content: 'Review and revoke sessions from the security page.',
  },
  {
    value: 'recovery',
    title: 'Recovery keys',
    content: 'Store recovery keys somewhere safe; each key bypasses two-factor sign-in once.',
    disabled: true,
  },
]

export function AccordionDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return <Accordion multiple defaultValue={['sign-in']} items={securityItems} className="w-full max-w-lg" />
  }
  return <Accordion defaultValue="sign-in" items={securityItems} className="w-full max-w-lg" />
}
```

### Multi-open and disabled

multiple allows any number of open items; disabled items cannot be toggled.

```jsx
import { Accordion } from '@kryv/teal'

const securityItems = [
  {
    value: 'sign-in',
    title: 'Sign-in notifications',
    content: 'Get alerted when a new device signs in to your account.',
  },
  {
    value: 'sessions',
    title: 'Active sessions',
    content: 'Review and revoke sessions from the security page.',
  },
  {
    value: 'recovery',
    title: 'Recovery keys',
    content: 'Store recovery keys somewhere safe; each key bypasses two-factor sign-in once.',
    disabled: true,
  },
]

export function AccordionDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return <Accordion multiple defaultValue={['sign-in']} items={securityItems} className="w-full max-w-lg" />
  }
  return <Accordion defaultValue="sign-in" items={securityItems} className="w-full max-w-lg" />
}
```

## Interface

### Accordion

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `items` (required) | `AccordionItem[]` | - | Items rendered by the accordion ({ value, title, content, disabled? }). |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Multi-open mode. value, defaultValue, and onValueChange are typed string in single mode and string[] when multiple is true. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` | - | - |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` | - | - |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` | - | - |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Toggles the focused item. |
| `Arrow Up` + `Arrow Down` | Moves focus between item triggers. |
| `Home` + `End` | Focuses the first or last trigger. |

- Implements the ARIA accordion pattern through the Radix primitive, with state exposed as aria-expanded on each trigger.
- Disabled items are skipped and cannot be toggled.
- The chevron is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

---

# Chip

A compact filter or selection token with an optional remove affordance.

## Usage

```js
import { Chip } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Chip label="Active only" selected onRemove={() => undefined} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Active filters or selections need compact, removable tokens.
### Avoid when

The status is informational only; use Badge.
### Behavior

The remove action is labeled from the chip text for screen readers.
### Responsive

Chips wrap in rows; keep labels to one or two words.

## Examples

### Removable filters

Selected chips tint primary; the remove button is labeled from the chip text.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Chip } from '@kryv/teal'

const initialTags = ['Design', 'Research', 'Planning']

export function ChipDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(initialTags)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        {tags.map((tag) => (
          <Chip key={tag} label={tag} onRemove={() => setTags((current) => current.filter((t) => t !== tag))} />
        ))}
        <Chip label="Locked" onRemove={() => undefined} disabled />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <Chip label="In progress" />
      <Chip label="Active filter" selected />
      <Chip label="Featured" variant="primary" />
      <Chip label="Archived" disabled />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Locked filters

Disabled chips communicate filters managed elsewhere.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Chip } from '@kryv/teal'

const initialTags = ['Design', 'Research', 'Planning']

export function ChipDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(initialTags)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        {tags.map((tag) => (
          <Chip key={tag} label={tag} onRemove={() => setTags((current) => current.filter((t) => t !== tag))} />
        ))}
        <Chip label="Locked" onRemove={() => undefined} disabled />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <Chip label="In progress" />
      <Chip label="Active filter" selected />
      <Chip label="Featured" variant="primary" />
      <Chip label="Archived" disabled />
    </div>
  )
}
```

# Kbd

An inline keyboard shortcut hint with a raised keycap treatment.

## Usage

```js
import { Kbd } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
Save with <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>S</Kbd>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A keyboard shortcut is referenced in help or onboarding copy.
### Avoid when

The key is part of a form value; use plain text.
### Behavior

Sizing is em-based so the keycap scales with its context.
### Responsive

Keep combinations short; wrap groups of keys with separators as text.

## Examples

### Shortcut hints

Kbd scales with surrounding text through em-based sizing.

```jsx
import { Kbd } from '@kryv/teal'

export function KbdDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3 text-sm">
      <p>
        Press <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd> to open the command palette.
      </p>
      <p>
        Use <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to close dialogs and <Kbd>Shift</Kbd> + <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> to add a new
        line.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Combinations

Join keys with plain-text separators for multi-key shortcuts.

```jsx
import { Kbd } from '@kryv/teal'

export function KbdDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3 text-sm">
      <p>
        Press <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd> to open the command palette.
      </p>
      <p>
        Use <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to close dialogs and <Kbd>Shift</Kbd> + <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> to add a new
        line.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

# Scroll Area

A scrollable region with styled, theme-consistent scrollbars.

## Usage

```js
import { ScrollArea } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ScrollArea maxHeight="16rem">
  <LongList />
</ScrollArea>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A panel needs a bounded height with theme-consistent scrollbars.
### Avoid when

The page itself should scroll; do not nest page-level scrolling.
### Behavior

The custom thumb appears over a transparent track only where scrolling is possible.
### Responsive

Set maxHeight in relative units so the region adapts to viewport height.

## Examples

### Bounded lists

Cap the height and the custom scrollbar appears only while scrolling is possible.

```jsx
import { ScrollArea } from '@kryv/teal'

const lists = [
  [
    'Avery Stone',
    'Blake Moreno',
    'Casey Nguyen',
    'Devon Patel',
    'Emery Kim',
    'Finley Ortiz',
    'Gray Lindqvist',
    'Harper Adeyemi',
    'Indigo Sato',
    'Jordan Ellis',
  ],
  [
    'Orion redesign',
    'Billing migration',
    'Mobile shell',
    'Reporting v2',
    'Access reviews',
    'Onboarding flow',
    'API gateway',
    'Design tokens',
    'Audit logging',
    'Search indexing',
  ],
]

export function ScrollAreaDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const items = lists[exampleIndex % lists.length]
  return (
    <ScrollArea maxHeight={220} className="w-72 rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/40">
      <ul className="divide-y divide-teal-outline-variant/40">
        {items.map((item) => (
          <li key={item} className="px-4 py-2.5 text-sm text-teal-on-surface">
            {item}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </ScrollArea>
  )
}
```

### Panel lists

Pair with a fixed maxHeight so the page itself keeps its own scroll.

```jsx
import { ScrollArea } from '@kryv/teal'

const lists = [
  [
    'Avery Stone',
    'Blake Moreno',
    'Casey Nguyen',
    'Devon Patel',
    'Emery Kim',
    'Finley Ortiz',
    'Gray Lindqvist',
    'Harper Adeyemi',
    'Indigo Sato',
    'Jordan Ellis',
  ],
  [
    'Orion redesign',
    'Billing migration',
    'Mobile shell',
    'Reporting v2',
    'Access reviews',
    'Onboarding flow',
    'API gateway',
    'Design tokens',
    'Audit logging',
    'Search indexing',
  ],
]

export function ScrollAreaDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const items = lists[exampleIndex % lists.length]
  return (
    <ScrollArea maxHeight={220} className="w-72 rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/40">
      <ul className="divide-y divide-teal-outline-variant/40">
        {items.map((item) => (
          <li key={item} className="px-4 py-2.5 text-sm text-teal-on-surface">
            {item}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </ScrollArea>
  )
}
```

# Code Block

A code panel with a language label, optional line numbers, and copy-to-clipboard.

## Usage

```js
import { CodeBlock } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<CodeBlock language="bash" code="npm install @kryv/teal" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Code or commands should be readable and copyable.
### Avoid when

A single identifier in prose; use inline code styling.
### Behavior

The copy action confirms with an icon swap and announces via its label.
### Responsive

Long lines scroll horizontally instead of wrapping.

## Examples

### Copy affordance

The copy button confirms with a check icon for two seconds.

```jsx
import { CodeBlock } from '@kryv/teal'

export function CodeBlockDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
        <CodeBlock
          language="tsx"
          showLineNumbers
          code={`import { Button } from '@kryv/teal'\n\nexport function SaveAction() {\n  return <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>\n}`}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <CodeBlock
        language="bash"
        code={`npm install @kryv/teal\nnpm run dev`}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Line numbers

Enable line numbers for walkthroughs that reference specific lines.

```jsx
import { CodeBlock } from '@kryv/teal'

export function CodeBlockDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
        <CodeBlock
          language="tsx"
          showLineNumbers
          code={`import { Button } from '@kryv/teal'\n\nexport function SaveAction() {\n  return <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>\n}`}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <CodeBlock
        language="bash"
        code={`npm install @kryv/teal\nnpm run dev`}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

# Dialog

A modal surface that owns focus management, naming, dismissal, and scroll locking.

## Usage

```js
import { Dialog } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open dialog</Button>
<Dialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Archive project?"
  description="The project can be restored later."
>
  <p>Project Orion will leave the active workspace.</p>
</Dialog>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A decision or focused task must temporarily block the page.
### Avoid when

The content can be inline or handled by a popover.
### Behavior

Focus is trapped, Escape dismisses, and focus returns to the trigger.
### Responsive

Use the built-in size and allow the body to scroll inside the panel.

## Examples

### Confirmation

Dialog traps focus, restores it on close, and dismisses with Escape or the scrim.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Dialog } from '@kryv/teal'

export function DialogDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>{exampleIndex ? 'Open confirmation dialog' : 'Open dialog'}</Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Archive project?"
        description="The project can be restored later."
        footer={
          <>
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Archive
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          Project Orion and its reports will leave the active workspace.
        </p>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Destructive confirmation

Use a danger action only when the consequence is clear and reversible where possible.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Dialog } from '@kryv/teal'

export function DialogDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>{exampleIndex ? 'Open confirmation dialog' : 'Open dialog'}</Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Archive project?"
        description="The project can be restored later."
        footer={
          <>
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Archive
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          Project Orion and its reports will leave the active workspace.
        </p>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Long-form task

For focused tasks, keep the title visible and let the dialog body own its scroll.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Dialog } from '@kryv/teal'

export function DialogDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>{exampleIndex ? 'Open confirmation dialog' : 'Open dialog'}</Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Archive project?"
        description="The project can be restored later."
        footer={
          <>
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Archive
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          Project Orion and its reports will leave the active workspace.
        </p>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Dialog

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Body content of the dialog. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes merged onto the dialog panel. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `Close` | Accessible label for the close button. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | - | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered under the title. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | - | Action area rendered at the bottom of the dialog. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the dialog opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state. |
| `restoreFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | - | Element that receives focus after a controlled dialog closes. |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` | Width of the dialog surface. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Title rendered at the top; also the accessible name of the dialog. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Escape` | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| `Tab` + `Shift+Tab` | Cycles focus through the focusable elements inside the dialog. |

- Renders role="dialog" with aria-modal, labelled by the title and described by the description.
- Focus moves into the dialog on open and is restored to the trigger on close.
- Background content is scroll-locked while the dialog is open.

---

# Tooltip

A short contextual hint with accessible trigger association and collision handling.

## Usage

```js
import { Tooltip, TooltipProvider, IconButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
// Mount once near the app root so tooltips share open-delay grouping
<TooltipProvider>
  <App />
</TooltipProvider>

// Per-instance delayDuration overrides the provider when needed
<Tooltip content="Refresh search results">
  <IconButton label="Refresh results">
    <Search />
  </IconButton>
</Tooltip>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

An unfamiliar icon or abbreviated label needs a brief hint.
### Avoid when

The user must read or interact with the content.
### Behavior

Hover and focus reveal a short non-interactive description.
### Responsive

Never rely on hover alone; provide a visible label on touch layouts.

## Examples

### Icon button hint

Tooltips label icon-only controls on hover and keyboard focus. Click the icon to expand the search field.

```jsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { IconButton, Input, Tooltip } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Search, X } from 'lucide-react'

export function TooltipDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const inputRef = useRef(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return undefined
    const frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => inputRef.current?.focus())
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(frame)
  }, [open])

  return (
    <div
      className={`relative flex items-center transition-[width] duration-200 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none ${
        open ? 'w-64' : 'w-10'
      }`}
    >
      {open ? (
        <div className="flex h-10 w-full items-center gap-1 rounded-full border border-teal-outline-variant/40 bg-teal-surface pl-3 pr-1 shadow-sm">
          <Search aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 shrink-0 text-teal-on-surface-variant" />
          <Input
            ref={inputRef}
            aria-label="Search"
            placeholder="Search..."
            onKeyDown={(event) => {
              if (event.key === 'Escape') setOpen(false)
            }}
            className="h-10 min-h-0 flex-1 rounded-none border-transparent bg-transparent px-2 py-0 text-sm shadow-none focus-visible:border-transparent focus-visible:ring-0"
          />
          <IconButton label="Close search" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
            <X />
          </IconButton>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <Tooltip content="Search" delayDuration={0}>
          <IconButton label="Open search" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
            <Search />
          </IconButton>
        </Tooltip>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Pure hover and focus hint

Use Tooltip for short, non-interactive context around an unfamiliar icon.

```jsx
import { IconButton, Tooltip } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Info } from 'lucide-react'

export function TooltipPureDemo() {
  return (
    <Tooltip content="Only visible context, never an action" delayDuration={0}>
      <IconButton label="More information">
        <Info />
      </IconButton>
    </Tooltip>
  )
}
```

### Action context

Keep the hint short when it sits beside an unfamiliar product action.

```jsx
import { IconButton, Tooltip } from '@kryv/teal'
import { CircleHelp } from 'lucide-react'

export function TooltipActionsDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <Tooltip content="Changes apply to everyone in this workspace" delayDuration={0}>
        <IconButton label="Workspace sharing help"><CircleHelp /></IconButton>
      </Tooltip>
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Workspace sharing</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Tooltip

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | - | Element the tooltip describes; receives trigger props automatically. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes merged onto the tooltip content. |
| `content` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Text rendered inside the tooltip. |
| `delayDuration` | `number` | - | Per-instance open delay in milliseconds; overrides the nearest TooltipProvider. |
| `side` | `enum` | `top` | Preferred side of the trigger for the tooltip. |

### TooltipProvider

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delayDuration` | `number` | `300` | Open delay in milliseconds shared by the grouped tooltips; moving between triggers skips the delay. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Focus` | Shows the tooltip when its trigger receives keyboard focus. |
| `Escape` | Dismisses the tooltip. |

- The trigger is described by the tooltip through aria-describedby.
- Tooltips are for short hints only; never place interactive content inside them.
- Wrap the app in TooltipProvider once so tooltips share open-delay grouping; moving between triggers then skips the delay.

---

# Menu

A structured action menu with keyboard navigation, disabled items, icons, and danger styling.

## Usage

```js
import { Menu, IconButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Menu
  trigger={<IconButton label="Project actions"><MoreVertical /></IconButton>}
  items={[
    { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', onSelect: () => undefined },
    { id: 'archive', label: 'Archive', variant: 'danger', onSelect: () => undefined },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Several related actions belong behind one trigger.
### Avoid when

The actions should remain visible for frequent workflows.
### Behavior

Keyboard navigation and dismissal are managed by Radix.
### Responsive

Keep destructive actions separated and easy to reach on touch.

## Examples

### Project actions

Items support icons, separators, and a danger variant for destructive actions.

```jsx
import { IconButton, Menu } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Archive, MoreVertical, Settings } from 'lucide-react'

export function MenuDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Menu
      trigger={
        <IconButton label={exampleIndex ? 'Additional actions' : 'Project actions'}>
          <MoreVertical />
        </IconButton>
      }
      items={[
        { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: <Settings />, onSelect: () => undefined },
        {
          id: 'archive',
          label: 'Archive',
          icon: <Archive />,
          variant: 'danger',
          separatorBefore: true,
          onSelect: () => undefined,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Separated destructive action

Keep destructive actions at the end of the menu behind a separator.

```jsx
import { IconButton, Menu } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Archive, MoreVertical, Settings } from 'lucide-react'

export function MenuDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Menu
      trigger={
        <IconButton label={exampleIndex ? 'Additional actions' : 'Project actions'}>
          <MoreVertical />
        </IconButton>
      }
      items={[
        { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: <Settings />, onSelect: () => undefined },
        {
          id: 'archive',
          label: 'Archive',
          icon: <Archive />,
          variant: 'danger',
          separatorBefore: true,
          onSelect: () => undefined,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Keyboard action menu

Menus preserve arrow-key navigation and Escape dismissal.

```jsx
import { IconButton, Menu } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Archive, MoreVertical, Settings } from 'lucide-react'

export function MenuDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Menu
      trigger={
        <IconButton label={exampleIndex ? 'Additional actions' : 'Project actions'}>
          <MoreVertical />
        </IconButton>
      }
      items={[
        { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: <Settings />, onSelect: () => undefined },
        {
          id: 'archive',
          label: 'Archive',
          icon: <Archive />,
          variant: 'danger',
          separatorBefore: true,
          onSelect: () => undefined,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Menu

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `enum` | `end` | Horizontal alignment of the menu relative to the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes merged onto the menu content. |
| `items` (required) | `MenuItem[]` | - | Items rendered in the menu. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Accessible name for the menu. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `false` | Traps focus and blocks outside interaction while open. Defaults to false. |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | - | Element that opens the menu; receives trigger props automatically. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` + `Arrow Down` | Opens the menu and highlights the first item. |
| `Arrow Up` | Opens the menu and highlights the last item. |
| `Arrow Up` + `Arrow Down` | Moves the highlight between items, skipping disabled ones. |
| `Home` + `End` | Highlights the first or last item. |
| `Typing` | Typeahead jumps to the first matching item. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the highlighted item and closes the menu. |
| `Escape` + `Tab` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. |

- Renders the ARIA menu pattern with menuitem roles and roving highlight.
- Icons are decorative; every item keeps a text label.
- Set modal to trap focus and block outside interaction while the menu is open.

---

# Popover

An anchored surface for arbitrary controls and supplemental content.

## Usage

```js
import { Popover, Button, Checkbox } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Popover label="Filter projects" trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Filters</Button>}>
  <div className="grid gap-3">
    <Checkbox label="Active only" defaultChecked />
    <Button size="sm">Apply filters</Button>
  </div>
</Popover>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Supplemental controls should stay anchored to a trigger.
### Avoid when

The content is a blocking task or a simple one-line hint.
### Behavior

Focus returns to the trigger after dismissal.
### Responsive

Keep panels within the viewport and avoid overly wide forms.

## Examples

### Filter panel

Popover anchors interactive content to a trigger with collision-aware placement.

```jsx
import { Button, Checkbox, Popover } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Filter } from 'lucide-react'

export function PopoverDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Popover
      label="Filter projects"
      trigger={
        <Button variant="secondary">
          <Filter /> {exampleIndex ? 'Refine projects' : 'Filters'}
        </Button>
      }
      align="start"
    >
      <div className="grid gap-3">
        <h3 className="font-teal-headline font-bold">Filter projects</h3>
        <Checkbox label="Active only" defaultChecked />
        <Button size="sm">Apply filters</Button>
      </div>
    </Popover>
  )
}
```

### Inline filters

Keep a small set of filters anchored to the toolbar that owns them.

```jsx
import { Button, Checkbox, Popover } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Filter } from 'lucide-react'

export function PopoverDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Popover
      label="Filter projects"
      trigger={
        <Button variant="secondary">
          <Filter /> {exampleIndex ? 'Refine projects' : 'Filters'}
        </Button>
      }
      align="start"
    >
      <div className="grid gap-3">
        <h3 className="font-teal-headline font-bold">Filter projects</h3>
        <Checkbox label="Active only" defaultChecked />
        <Button size="sm">Apply filters</Button>
      </div>
    </Popover>
  )
}
```

### Supplemental controls

Use a popover for controls that do not deserve a full route or dialog.

```jsx
import { Button, Checkbox, Popover } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Filter } from 'lucide-react'

export function PopoverDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Popover
      label="Filter projects"
      trigger={
        <Button variant="secondary">
          <Filter /> {exampleIndex ? 'Refine projects' : 'Filters'}
        </Button>
      }
      align="start"
    >
      <div className="grid gap-3">
        <h3 className="font-teal-headline font-bold">Filter projects</h3>
        <Checkbox label="Active only" defaultChecked />
        <Button size="sm">Apply filters</Button>
      </div>
    </Popover>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Popover

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `enum` | `center` | Horizontal alignment of the content relative to the trigger. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Content rendered inside the popover surface. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes merged onto the popover content. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | - | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `label` (required) | `string` | - | Accessible name for the dialog-like popover surface. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the popover opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state. |
| `side` | `enum` | `bottom` | Side of the trigger the content opens on. |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | - | Element that toggles the popover; receives trigger props automatically. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Escape` | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. |
| `Tab` | Moves focus into the popover content, then back into the page flow. |

- The trigger exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls for the popover content.
- Focus is not trapped; popovers suit small control panels, not multi-step flows.
- Placement flips automatically to stay inside the viewport.

---

# Drawer

A slide-over panel for focused side tasks, built on the dialog focus model.

## Usage

```js
import { Drawer, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Drawer
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Project settings"
  side="right"
>
  <SettingsForm />
</Drawer>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A focused side task needs more room than a dialog but should not navigate away.
### Avoid when

The task is a simple confirmation; use Dialog.
### Behavior

Focus is trapped and restored, Escape dismisses, and the panel slides from the chosen edge.
### Responsive

The default width caps at the viewport; forms inside own their own scroll.

## Examples

### Side panel

The drawer slides from either edge and traps focus like a dialog.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Drawer } from '@kryv/teal'

export function DrawerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const side = exampleIndex ? 'left' : 'right'
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        {exampleIndex ? 'Open left drawer' : 'Open drawer'}
      </Button>
      <Drawer
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        side={side}
        title="Project details"
        description="Orion workspace — updated 2 hours ago"
        footer={
          <>
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Save changes</Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          Manage members, integrations, and archive rules for this project without leaving the current page.
        </p>
      </Drawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Left edge

Use side="left" when the panel continues a left-side navigation context.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Drawer } from '@kryv/teal'

export function DrawerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const side = exampleIndex ? 'left' : 'right'
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        {exampleIndex ? 'Open left drawer' : 'Open drawer'}
      </Button>
      <Drawer
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        side={side}
        title="Project details"
        description="Orion workspace — updated 2 hours ago"
        footer={
          <>
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Save changes</Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          Manage members, integrations, and archive rules for this project without leaving the current page.
        </p>
      </Drawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

# Hover Card

A rich preview surface revealed on hover or focus, for context without navigation.

## Usage

```js
import { HoverCard, Link } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<HoverCard trigger={<Link href="/projects/orion">Orion</Link>}>
  <ProjectSummary />
</HoverCard>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Rich preview context helps before committing to navigation.
### Avoid when

The content is a short hint; use Tooltip, or must be interacted with on touch; use Popover.
### Behavior

Hover and keyboard focus open the card after a tunable delay.
### Responsive

Provide the same content through another path on touch layouts.

## Examples

### Preview on hover

Delays are tunable; keyboard focus opens the card too.

```jsx
import { HoverCard } from '@kryv/teal'

export function HoverCardDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const person = exampleIndex
    ? { handle: '@blake', name: 'Blake Moreno', role: 'Engineering — Platform team' }
    : { handle: '@avery', name: 'Avery Stone', role: 'Design lead — Workspace team' }
  return (
    <HoverCard
      trigger={
        <button type="button" className="font-semibold text-teal-primary underline underline-offset-2">
          {person.handle}
        </button>
      }
    >
      <div className="space-y-1">
        <p className="text-sm font-bold text-teal-on-surface">{person.name}</p>
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">{person.role}</p>
      </div>
    </HoverCard>
  )
}
```

### Identity preview

Show a person or project summary without leaving the list.

```jsx
import { HoverCard } from '@kryv/teal'

export function HoverCardDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const person = exampleIndex
    ? { handle: '@blake', name: 'Blake Moreno', role: 'Engineering — Platform team' }
    : { handle: '@avery', name: 'Avery Stone', role: 'Design lead — Workspace team' }
  return (
    <HoverCard
      trigger={
        <button type="button" className="font-semibold text-teal-primary underline underline-offset-2">
          {person.handle}
        </button>
      }
    >
      <div className="space-y-1">
        <p className="text-sm font-bold text-teal-on-surface">{person.name}</p>
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">{person.role}</p>
      </div>
    </HoverCard>
  )
}
```

# Command

A command palette dialog with grouped, filterable actions and keyboard navigation.

## Usage

```js
import { Command, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Command
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  groups={[
    { label: 'Projects', items: [{ id: 'orion', label: 'Open Orion', onSelect: () => undefined }] },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Power users need fast keyboard access to many actions.
### Avoid when

There are few actions; use visible buttons or a Menu.
### Behavior

Filtering, highlight, and selection reset on every open.
### Responsive

The panel caps at viewport width with its own internal scroll.

## Examples

### Palette

Arrows cycle filtered items, Enter runs the action, state resets on open.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Command } from '@kryv/teal'
import { FilePlus2, FolderPen, Rocket, Settings, Trash2, UserPlus } from 'lucide-react'

export function CommandDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [lastAction, setLastAction] = useState('')

  function run(label) {
    setLastAction(label)
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
          Open admin commands
        </Button>
        {lastAction ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">Last action: {lastAction}</p> : null}
        <Command
          open={open}
          onOpenChange={setOpen}
          placeholder="Search admin commands…"
          emptyMessage="No admin commands match"
          groups={[
            {
              label: 'Workspace',
              items: [
                { id: 'invite', label: 'Invite member', hint: '⌘I', icon: <UserPlus />, onSelect: () => run('Invite member') },
                { id: 'settings', label: 'Workspace settings', icon: <Settings />, onSelect: () => run('Workspace settings') },
              ],
            },
            {
              label: 'Danger zone',
              items: [
                { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete workspace', icon: <Trash2 />, onSelect: () => run('Delete workspace') },
              ],
            },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open command palette</Button>
      {lastAction ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">Last action: {lastAction}</p> : null}
      <Command
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        groups={[
          {
            label: 'Project',
            items: [
              { id: 'new', label: 'New project', hint: '⌘N', icon: <FilePlus2 />, onSelect: () => run('New project') },
              { id: 'rename', label: 'Rename project', icon: <FolderPen />, onSelect: () => run('Rename project') },
              { id: 'deploy', label: 'Deploy to production', hint: '⌘D', icon: <Rocket />, onSelect: () => run('Deploy to production') },
            ],
          },
          {
            label: 'Workspace',
            items: [
              { id: 'invite', label: 'Invite member', hint: '⌘I', icon: <UserPlus />, onSelect: () => run('Invite member') },
              { id: 'settings', label: 'Workspace settings', icon: <Settings />, onSelect: () => run('Workspace settings') },
            ],
          },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Keyboard first

Bind a global shortcut to open the palette; keep item hints scannable.

```jsx

          Open admin commands
        </Button>
        {lastAction ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">Last action: {lastAction}</p> : null}
        <Command
          open={open}
          onOpenChange={setOpen}
          placeholder="Search admin commands…"
          emptyMessage="No admin commands match"
          groups={[
            {
              label: 'Workspace',
              items: [
                { id: 'invite', label: 'Invite member', hint: '⌘I', icon: <UserPlus />, onSelect: () => run('Invite member') },
                { id: 'settings', label: 'Workspace settings', icon: <Settings />, onSelect: () => run('Workspace settings') },
              ],
            },
            {
              label: 'Danger zone',
              items: [
                { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete workspace', icon: <Trash2 />, onSelect: () => run('Delete workspace') },

          ]}
        />
      </div>

  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">

      <Command
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        groups={[
          {
            label: 'Project',
            items: [
              { id: 'new', label: 'New project', hint: '⌘N', icon: <FilePlus2 />, onSelect: () => run('New project') },
```

# Toast

Imperative, announced feedback with semantic variants, optional actions, and dismissal.

## Usage

```js
import { Toaster, toast } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
// Mount once near the app root
<Toaster />

// Call toast() from anywhere
toast({ title: 'Changes saved', variant: 'success' })
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A completed or failed action needs brief asynchronous feedback.
### Avoid when

The message is required to continue or must be read in context.
### Behavior

Toaster announces messages and supports timed or manual dismissal.
### Responsive

Position toasts away from mobile browser controls and safe areas.

## Examples

### Saving feedback

Call toast() from anywhere once a Toaster is mounted near the app root.

```jsx
import { Button, toast } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ToastDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
      toast({ title: exampleIndex ? 'Review saved' : 'Changes saved', description: 'Your settings are up to date.', variant: 'success' })
      }
    >
      {exampleIndex ? 'Show review toast' : 'Show toast'}
    </Button>
  )
}
```

### Failure feedback

Use a danger variant for a failed action and keep the recovery path in context.

```jsx
import { Button, toast } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ToastDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
      toast({ title: exampleIndex ? 'Review saved' : 'Changes saved', description: 'Your settings are up to date.', variant: 'success' })
      }
    >
      {exampleIndex ? 'Show review toast' : 'Show toast'}
    </Button>
  )
}
```

### Undo feedback

Offer a short action when users may want to reverse a completed operation.

```jsx
import { Button, toast } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ToastDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
      toast({ title: exampleIndex ? 'Review saved' : 'Changes saved', description: 'Your settings are up to date.', variant: 'success' })
      }
    >
      {exampleIndex ? 'Show review toast' : 'Show toast'}
    </Button>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Toaster

_This module forwards native element properties._

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `F8` | Moves focus to the toast viewport so toasts can be reviewed and dismissed. |
| `Escape` | Dismisses the focused toast. |
| `Swipe right` | Dismisses a toast on touch devices. |

- Toasts are announced through a live region as they appear.
- Actions render as real buttons with accessible labels.
- Pass duration: Infinity for critical messages that must be dismissed manually.

---

# Empty State

An explanatory empty result with an optional action and SVG icon.

## Usage

```js
import { EmptyState, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<EmptyState
  title="No reports"
  description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
  action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A product surface has no results or has not been configured.
### Avoid when

Content is merely loading or filtered temporarily.
### Behavior

Explain what happened and give one clear next action when useful.
### Responsive

Keep the message readable and center the action beneath it.

## Examples

### First-run

Pair a short explanation with a single primary action.

```jsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EmptyStateDemo() {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      title="No reports"
      description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
      action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
    />
  )
}
```

### Filtered empty result

Explain that filters produced no results and offer a way to adjust them.

```jsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EmptyStateDemo() {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      title="No reports"
      description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
      action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
    />
  )
}
```

## Interface

### EmptyState

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | - | Call to action rendered below the description. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text that explains the empty state. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon rendered above the title. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Short heading for the empty state. |
| `titleAs` | `enum` | `"h3"` | Heading element used for the title; defaults to 'h3'. Adjust to fit the page outline. |

## Accessibility

- The title renders as an h3 by default; adjust titleAs so the empty state fits the page outline.
- The action is a real button or link; keep to a single primary action.

# Loading

Named progress and loading treatments for local, skeleton, and full-surface states.

## Usage

```js
import { Spinner, Progress, Skeleton, LoadingState } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Spinner label="Saving" />
<Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-40" />
<LoadingState label="Loading reports" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users need feedback while content or work is in progress.
### Avoid when

The operation is instant or no meaningful progress exists.
### Behavior

Use Spinner for local work, Skeleton for layout, and Progress for measurable work.
### Responsive

Prefer local indicators so small screens retain useful content.

## Examples

### Loading treatments

Spinner and Progress for active work, Skeleton for layout placeholders, LoadingState for regions.

```jsx
import { LoadingState, Progress, Skeleton, Spinner } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LoadingDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-5">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-5">
        <Spinner label="Loading example" />
        <Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
      </div>
      <Skeleton className="h-20 w-full" />
      <LoadingState label="Loading reports" className="min-h-32" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Skeleton region

Reserve the eventual layout with Skeleton when content shape is known.

```jsx
import { LoadingState, Progress, Skeleton, Spinner } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LoadingDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-5">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-5">
        <Spinner label="Loading example" />
        <Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
      </div>
      <Skeleton className="h-20 w-full" />
      <LoadingState label="Loading reports" className="min-h-32" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### LoadingState

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label announced by screen readers while the region is loading. |

### Spinner

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label announced by screen readers. |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` | Diameter of the spinner. |

### Skeleton

_This module forwards native element properties._

### Progress

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label describing what the progress bar measures. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Merges the component onto its child element instead of rendering the default element (Radix Slot). |
| `value` | `number \| null` | `0` | Current progress, clamped between 0 and max. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | Maximum value used to compute the filled percentage. |

## Accessibility

- Spinner and LoadingState render role="status" with an accessible label, announced once to screen readers.
- Progress exposes aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax through the Radix progress primitive.
- Skeleton is aria-hidden because it duplicates content that is about to load.
- All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion.

---

# Alert

An inline feedback banner with semantic variants, an optional title, and dismissal.

## Usage

```js
import { Alert } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Alert variant="warning" title="Payment method expiring">
  The workspace card ends in 04/25. Update billing details to avoid interruption.
</Alert>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Feedback must stay visible in context until it is read or dismissed.
### Avoid when

A brief confirmation is enough; use a toast for transient feedback.
### Behavior

Danger renders role="alert" for immediate announcement; other variants render role="status".
### Responsive

Let the body text wrap and keep the title to a short phrase.

## Examples

### Variants

Semantic variants pair a standard icon with a matching surface treatment.

```jsx
import { Alert } from '@kryv/teal'

export function AlertDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Alert
        variant="warning"
        title="Payment method expiring"
        onDismiss={() => undefined}
        className="w-full max-w-lg"
      >
        The workspace card ends in 04/25. Update billing details to avoid interruption.
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
      <Alert variant="success" title="Report published">
        The quarterly security report is now available to all workspace members.
      </Alert>
      <Alert variant="danger" title="Sign-in blocked">
        We stopped a sign-in attempt from an unrecognized device.
      </Alert>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Dismissible

Pass onDismiss to render a close button for feedback the user can clear.

```jsx
import { Alert } from '@kryv/teal'

export function AlertDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Alert
        variant="warning"
        title="Payment method expiring"
        onDismiss={() => undefined}
        className="w-full max-w-lg"
      >
        The workspace card ends in 04/25. Update billing details to avoid interruption.
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
      <Alert variant="success" title="Report published">
        The quarterly security report is now available to all workspace members.
      </Alert>
      <Alert variant="danger" title="Sign-in blocked">
        We stopped a sign-in attempt from an unrecognized device.
      </Alert>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Interface

### Alert

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon override; defaults to the variant's standard icon. Always hidden from assistive technology. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | - | Renders a dismiss button and calls this when it is pressed. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | - | Bold leading text of the alert. |
| `variant` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| null` | `"info"` | Semantic treatment of the banner. |

## Accessibility

- Danger renders role="alert" so the message is announced immediately; other variants render role="status".
- The variant icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; meaning is carried by the text.
- The dismiss control is a labeled button in the normal tab order.

---

# Notification Item

A sanitized ecosystem inbox row with severity, source application, read state, deep link, and delivery-state controls.

## Usage

```js
import { NotificationItem } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<NotificationItem
  severity="warning"
  appLabel="Yang Operations"
  timestamp="2 hours ago"
  title="photos-api restarted unexpectedly"
  href="https://yang.example/incidents/photos-api"
  onMute={() => undefined}
  onArchive={() => undefined}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

An inbox lists sanitized pointers to application events.
### Avoid when

The feedback is local to the current task; use Alert or Toast instead.
### Behavior

Mute and archive touch delivery state only; the deep link never mutates the source.
### Responsive

Text wraps and controls stay reachable at mobile widths.

## Examples

### Unread with controls

Unread items are emphasized and announced; mute and archive only touch delivery state, never the source event.

```jsx
import { NotificationItem } from '@kryv/teal'

export function NotificationItemDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="success"
      appLabel="Photos"
      timestamp="just now"
      title="Import finished"
      href="https://photos.kryvlabs.example/imports/1"
      read
    />
  ) : (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="warning"
      appLabel="Yang Operations"
      timestamp="2 hours ago"
      title="photos-api restarted unexpectedly"
      href="https://yang.kryvlabs.example/incidents/photos-api"
      onMute={() => undefined}
      onArchive={() => undefined}
    />
  )
}
```

### Read

Read items drop the emphasis and the unread announcement.

```jsx
import { NotificationItem } from '@kryv/teal'

export function NotificationItemDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="success"
      appLabel="Photos"
      timestamp="just now"
      title="Import finished"
      href="https://photos.kryvlabs.example/imports/1"
      read
    />
  ) : (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="warning"
      appLabel="Yang Operations"
      timestamp="2 hours ago"
      title="photos-api restarted unexpectedly"
      href="https://yang.kryvlabs.example/incidents/photos-api"
      onMute={() => undefined}
      onArchive={() => undefined}
    />
  )
}
```

# Health Indicator

An explicit ecosystem health status that reports unknown and stale evidence instead of implying health.

## Usage

```js
import { HealthIndicator } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<HealthIndicator status="healthy" label="Photos" />
<HealthIndicator status="unknown" label="Trict" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A surface reports one application or ecosystem health status.
### Avoid when

The status is decorative; omit it instead of implying health.
### Behavior

Unknown, stale, and checking are explicit states; health is never inferred from missing evidence.
### Responsive

The badge and label wrap naturally in compact headers.

## Examples

### Reported statuses

Healthy, degraded, and down come straight from source evidence.

```jsx
import { HealthIndicator } from '@kryv/teal'

export function HealthIndicatorDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="stale" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="unknown" label="Trict" />
      <HealthIndicator status="loading" label="Yang Operations" />
    </div>
  ) : (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="healthy" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="degraded" label="Yang Operations" />
      <HealthIndicator status="down" label="Trict" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Missing evidence

Stale, unknown, and checking states stay visible; health is never inferred.

```jsx
import { HealthIndicator } from '@kryv/teal'

export function HealthIndicatorDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="stale" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="unknown" label="Trict" />
      <HealthIndicator status="loading" label="Yang Operations" />
    </div>
  ) : (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="healthy" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="degraded" label="Yang Operations" />
      <HealthIndicator status="down" label="Trict" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

# Step-Up Notice

An inline warning that explains a required fresh verification and hosts the caller’s verification action.

## Usage

```js
import { StepUpNotice, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<StepUpNotice
  title="Confirm it's you"
  action={<Button size="sm">Verify with passkey</Button>}
>
  Approving a repair requires fresh verification.
</StepUpNotice>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A sensitive action requires fresh strong authentication first.
### Avoid when

A plain warning suffices; use Alert instead.
### Behavior

The verification action is caller-supplied; the notice never starts or auto-submits verification.
### Responsive

The action wraps beneath the explanation on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Verification required

The action is caller-supplied; the notice never starts verification on its own.

```jsx
import { Button, StepUpNotice } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StepUpNoticeDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <StepUpNotice title="Session expiring" onDismiss={() => undefined}>
      Verify again to keep this session active.
    </StepUpNotice>
  ) : (
    <StepUpNotice
      title="Confirm it's you"
      action={<Button size="sm">Verify with passkey</Button>}
    >
      Approving a repair requires fresh verification before Yang continues.
    </StepUpNotice>
  )
}
```

### Dismissible

Pass onDismiss when the notice is informational rather than blocking.

```jsx
import { Button, StepUpNotice } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StepUpNoticeDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <StepUpNotice title="Session expiring" onDismiss={() => undefined}>
      Verify again to keep this session active.
    </StepUpNotice>
  ) : (
    <StepUpNotice
      title="Confirm it's you"
      action={<Button size="sm">Verify with passkey</Button>}
    >
      Approving a repair requires fresh verification before Yang continues.
    </StepUpNotice>
  )
}
```

# Banner

A page-level notice strip for workspace-wide feedback that owns the top of a view.

## Usage

```js
import { Banner, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Banner variant="warning" title="Scheduled maintenance">
  The workspace is read-only on Saturday, 02:00–03:00 UTC.
</Banner>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Feedback applies to the entire view, not one field or task.
### Avoid when

The message is local to a control or a transient confirmation; use Field, Alert, or Toast.
### Behavior

Danger renders role="alert" for immediate announcement; other variants render role="status".
### Responsive

The action wraps beneath the message on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Page-level feedback

A stronger accent than Alert, for notices that apply to the whole view.

```jsx
import { Banner, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BannerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Banner
        variant="warning"
        title="Trial ends in 7 days"
        action={<Button size="sm">Upgrade plan</Button>}
        onDismiss={() => undefined}
        className="max-w-2xl"
      >
        Upgrade to keep unlimited projects and priority support for the whole workspace.
      </Banner>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-3">
      <Banner variant="info" title="Scheduled maintenance">
        The workspace will be read-only on Sunday from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.
      </Banner>
      <Banner variant="success" title="Migration complete">
        All projects were moved to the new region without downtime.
      </Banner>
      <Banner variant="danger" title="Storage limit reached" onDismiss={() => undefined}>
        New uploads are paused until you free up space or upgrade the plan.
      </Banner>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Dismissible notices

Pass onDismiss for notices the user can clear for the session.

```jsx
import { Banner, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BannerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Banner
        variant="warning"
        title="Trial ends in 7 days"
        action={<Button size="sm">Upgrade plan</Button>}
        onDismiss={() => undefined}
        className="max-w-2xl"
      >
        Upgrade to keep unlimited projects and priority support for the whole workspace.
      </Banner>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-3">
      <Banner variant="info" title="Scheduled maintenance">
        The workspace will be read-only on Sunday from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.
      </Banner>
      <Banner variant="success" title="Migration complete">
        All projects were moved to the new region without downtime.
      </Banner>
      <Banner variant="danger" title="Storage limit reached" onDismiss={() => undefined}>
        New uploads are paused until you free up space or upgrade the plan.
      </Banner>
    </div>
  )
}
```

# Progress Circle

A radial progress indicator with determinate and indeterminate modes.

## Usage

```js
import { ProgressCircle } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ProgressCircle value={64} label="Import progress" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Progress needs a compact radial treatment.
### Avoid when

A precise value matters in a table; use Progress.
### Behavior

Determinate mode exposes aria-valuenow; omit value for indeterminate.
### Responsive

Set an explicit size per context instead of scaling.

## Examples

### Radial progress

role="progressbar" carries the value; omit value for a spinning indeterminate arc.

```jsx
import { ProgressCircle } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ProgressCircleDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ProgressCircle size={72} strokeWidth={7} value={82} label="Storage used" />
        <ProgressCircle size={72} strokeWidth={7} label="Syncing files" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <ProgressCircle value={25} label="Quarter progress" />
      <ProgressCircle value={64} label="Upload progress" />
      <ProgressCircle value={100} label="Backup complete" />
      <ProgressCircle label="Loading reports" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Indeterminate work

Omit value while progress cannot be measured.

```jsx
import { ProgressCircle } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ProgressCircleDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ProgressCircle size={72} strokeWidth={7} value={82} label="Storage used" />
        <ProgressCircle size={72} strokeWidth={7} label="Syncing files" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <ProgressCircle value={25} label="Quarter progress" />
      <ProgressCircle value={64} label="Upload progress" />
      <ProgressCircle value={100} label="Backup complete" />
      <ProgressCircle label="Loading reports" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

# Timeline

A vertical activity feed with tone dots, connectors, and timestamps.

## Usage

```js
import { Timeline } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Timeline
  items={[
    { id: '1', title: 'Deploy finished', timestamp: '2 min ago', tone: 'success' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Events form a chronological feed.
### Avoid when

Items are peers without time order; use a plain list.
### Behavior

Tone dots carry semantics; connectors skip the last item.
### Responsive

Content wraps while the rail stays fixed width.

## Examples

### Activity feed

Tone dots mark event semantics; connectors link the sequence.

```jsx
import { Timeline } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimelineDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
        <Timeline
          items={[
            { id: 'queued', title: 'Deploy queued', description: 'Release 2.4.0 · web-app', timestamp: '09:41', tone: 'neutral' },
            { id: 'building', title: 'Build completed', description: '412 modules in 3m 12s', timestamp: '09:46', tone: 'primary' },
            { id: 'live', title: 'Release is live', description: 'Health checks passing', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <Timeline
        items={[
          { id: 'commit', title: 'Jonas pushed 3 commits', description: 'feat: billing usage export', timestamp: '08:15', tone: 'neutral' },
          { id: 'review', title: 'Review approved', description: 'Priya approved #482', timestamp: '08:47', tone: 'primary' },
          { id: 'deploy', title: 'Deployed to production', description: 'Release 2.4.0 is live', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          { id: 'alert', title: 'Error budget warning', description: 'checkout-api above 2% errors', timestamp: '10:03', tone: 'warning' },
          { id: 'rollback', title: 'Rollback triggered', description: 'Reverted to 2.3.9', timestamp: '10:11', tone: 'danger' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Event tones

Use success and warning tones to mark outcomes in a feed.

```jsx
import { Timeline } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimelineDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
        <Timeline
          items={[
            { id: 'queued', title: 'Deploy queued', description: 'Release 2.4.0 · web-app', timestamp: '09:41', tone: 'neutral' },
            { id: 'building', title: 'Build completed', description: '412 modules in 3m 12s', timestamp: '09:46', tone: 'primary' },
            { id: 'live', title: 'Release is live', description: 'Health checks passing', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <Timeline
        items={[
          { id: 'commit', title: 'Jonas pushed 3 commits', description: 'feat: billing usage export', timestamp: '08:15', tone: 'neutral' },
          { id: 'review', title: 'Review approved', description: 'Priya approved #482', timestamp: '08:47', tone: 'primary' },
          { id: 'deploy', title: 'Deployed to production', description: 'Release 2.4.0 is live', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          { id: 'alert', title: 'Error budget warning', description: 'checkout-api above 2% errors', timestamp: '10:03', tone: 'warning' },
          { id: 'rollback', title: 'Rollback triggered', description: 'Reverted to 2.3.9', timestamp: '10:11', tone: 'danger' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

# App Switcher

An entitlement-filtered application switcher with an explicit Home destination and keyboard navigation.

## Usage

```js
import { AppSwitcher, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<AppSwitcher
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Switch application</Button>}
  homeHref="https://home.example"
  homeLabel="Home"
  apps={[
    { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: 'https://yang.example' },
    { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: 'https://photos.example', current: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

People move between entitled ecosystem applications.
### Avoid when

The navigation is inside one application; use vertical nav or tabs instead.
### Behavior

The caller filters applications by entitlement first; the switcher always includes the explicit Home destination.
### Responsive

The dropdown collision-handles to stay on screen; keep labels short on narrow layouts.

## Examples

### Household applications

The caller filters applications by entitlement first; the switcher renders only what it is given plus the explicit Home destination.

```jsx
import { AppSwitcher, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Camera, Gauge, LineChart } from 'lucide-react'

export function AppSwitcherDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <AppSwitcher
      trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Switch application</Button>}
      homeHref="https://home.kryvlabs.example"
      homeLabel="Home"
      apps={
        exampleIndex
          ? [{ id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: 'https://yang.kryvlabs.example', icon: <Gauge /> }]
          : [
              { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: 'https://yang.kryvlabs.example', icon: <Gauge /> },
              { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: 'https://photos.kryvlabs.example', icon: <Camera /> },
              { id: 'trict', label: 'Trict', href: 'https://trict.kryvlabs.example', icon: <LineChart />, current: true },
            ]
      }
    />
  )
}
```

### Single application

A member with one entitled application still gets the explicit Home destination.

```jsx
import { AppSwitcher, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Camera, Gauge, LineChart } from 'lucide-react'

export function AppSwitcherDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <AppSwitcher
      trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Switch application</Button>}
      homeHref="https://home.kryvlabs.example"
      homeLabel="Home"
      apps={
        exampleIndex
          ? [{ id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: 'https://yang.kryvlabs.example', icon: <Gauge /> }]
          : [
              { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: 'https://yang.kryvlabs.example', icon: <Gauge /> },
              { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: 'https://photos.kryvlabs.example', icon: <Camera /> },
              { id: 'trict', label: 'Trict', href: 'https://trict.kryvlabs.example', icon: <LineChart />, current: true },
            ]
      }
    />
  )
}
```
